solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mole sees ape trapping 'awks, perhaps?

indicators.note: trapping says one word holds the other inside it, as a snare holds its catch

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate
hawks are hunters; with the h dropped in cockney style, 'awks become 'unters

explanation.surface: Someone sees a monkey catching some birds of prey, dropped aitches and all.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'awks is the hint: drop the H from a synonym of hawks the same way, so hunters become 'UNTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: In espionage slang a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation, and an agent working against enemy spies is a similar figure.

clue.text: Free spirit after cannabis primarily, joints his speciality?

indicators.note: after places the free-spirit word behind the cannabis letter
primarily asks for the opening letter of the word cannabis

parts.note: a hippy is a free-spirited nonconformist

explanation.surface: A free-spirited hippy whose speciality is rolling cannabis joints.
explanation.walkthrough: The joints in the definition are carpentry joints, not cannabis; CHIPPY is British slang for a carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter, nicknamed with this slang term in Britain, makes woodwork joints as the core of the trade.

clue.text: Bird catching tear standing for the judge

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing means the assembled letters are set upright, reading from the bottom
catching says the bird word holds the tear word inside it

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
a tear is a rip

explanation.surface: A bird snagging a tear while standing in for a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns the whole container upside down, since in a down light standing up means reading from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports official who rules on play acts as a judge of the game.

clue.text: Forge taking sort of implement to be held over the fire

definitions.text: implement to be held over the fire

indicators.note: to forge is to hammer metal into a new shape, so these letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's forge produces a kind of tool for holding over flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forge' reads as a noun, the smithy, but works as a verb telling you to reshape TAKING SORT OF; 'sort of' is fodder, not a vague qualifier.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled fork used to brown bread over flames is held over an open hearth.

clue.text: True length of film broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is said out loud, so we take its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a reel is a spool holding a length of film

explanation.surface: An honest measure of how long a film was when it went out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine, true and actual are near synonyms describing something that is not fake.

clue.text: Reused manuscript, as father misspelt 'misspelt'!

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: misspelt says the quoted word that follows has its letters written in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Dad writes the word misspelt, and of course spells it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs: the first 'misspelt' is the instruction, the quoted 'misspelt' is the letters it scrambles.
explanation.definitionFit: A parchment scraped and written over again, with earlier text still faintly visible, is the classic recycled document.

clue.text: Bull's first charge knocked over cow

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word Bull's
knocked over in an across clue means the word is laid the other way, read backwards

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: A charging bull topples a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage the word names an ox or cow kept for meat, plural beeves, so a cow is an example.

clue.text: Sheep initially born masculine, we brought up those of another gender?

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the letters are raised, reading from the bottom upward
initially asks for the opening letters of the words Sheep and born

parts.note: masculine means male

explanation.surface: Sheep born male are raised by us as though they were the other sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns the whole string SBMALEWE upside down in this down light. The definition plays on the clue's 'masculine': young female sheep are of the other gender.
explanation.definitionFit: Young female sheep are the opposite sex to the masculine animals the surface mentions, hence another gender.

clue.text: Third of gifts brought down is opened

indicators.note: Third of asks for the letter in position three of the word gifts

parts.note: to lower something is to bring it down

explanation.surface: Presents get carried downstairs and unwrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that has bloomed has opened its buds, so blossomed and opened are synonyms.

clue.text: Merciless message by the devil, heart of clay

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: heart of asks for the central letters of the word clay

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a message

explanation.surface: A pitiless note from Satan, whose heart is made of clay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot be appeased or pacified shows no mercy, so unappeasable and pitiless are synonyms.

clue.text: Note a passage from some movement

indicators.note: passage from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few bars of music lifted from part of a symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' and 'movement' suggest music, but the note is a short written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written reminder or office communication is a note.

clue.text: Managing directors step on old vehicle

parts.note: running a firm means managing it
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Company bosses tread on a vintage car.
explanation.definitionFit: Old cars had a footboard below the doors, a step for getting in and out.

clue.text: One into social correspondence

indicators.note: into says the one-letter word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a social is a party, a gathering
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone joins in a sociable exchange of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' suggests letters, but here it means matching or equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence in the sense of agreement or equality between things is a synonym of equivalence.

clue.text: Take off a member, put in a friend

indicators.note: in says the word put sits inside the friend word

parts.note: mate is British slang for a friend

explanation.surface: Remove a member of a club and install a friend in their place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off a member' reads like expelling someone from a club; the member is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon cuts off a limb, and limbs are the body's members, so this is a precise paraphrase.

clue.text: Battered eel I seldom miss!

definitions.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman

indicators.note: battered means knocked about, so these letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A fish-and-chip lover says they rarely pass up battered eel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a verb, to forgo; it is the noun, a young lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived term for a young unmarried lady matches a miss; it is also a name for a damselfly.

clue.text: Excessive — so expensive?

definitions.meaning: a price that is too high is called unfair or exorbitant

explanation.definitionFit: Exorbitant demands and overpriced goods are both described as going beyond what is fair or sensible.

clue.text: Rodent collecting skin of snake for monkey

indicators.note: collecting says the rodent word gathers the other letters inside it

parts.note: the marmot is a large burrowing rodent

indicators.note: skin of asks for the outside letters of the word snake

explanation.surface: A rodent gathers snakeskin to trade for a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A small South American primate with a long tail and silky fur is a kind of monkey.

clue.text: Growing beautiful

definitions.meaning: growing in the sense of turning into, as in growing old
flattering or attractive, as a dress that suits the wearer

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the present participle of the verb meaning turn into, and an adjective for flattering and attractive.

clue.text: When one may seek the other?

definitions.text: When one may seek the other?

parts.words: When one may seek the other?
parts.note: 'the other' is slang for sex, so this asks at what point in life someone may lawfully look for it

explanation.definitionFit: The legal minimum age for sexual relations is the point at which someone may lawfully pursue a partner.

clue.text: Parade a design that's personal

definitions.meaning: a military display or parade, such as the Edinburgh military one
an inked design on the skin is about as personal as a design gets

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an outdoor military display and an inked picture made on someone's skin.

clue.text: Half of red wine red? That's not right — is it white?

indicators.note: half of says only one of the two halves of the wine's name is kept, here the back half

parts.note: burgundy is a red wine from eastern France

indicators.note: not right means the letter standing for right is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether a half-red wine is really white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' trims BURGUNDY to UNDY; 'not right' takes R from RED to leave ED. R for right is standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth left in its natural state is often a pale, whitish colour.

clue.text: Monroe is recollected as a phenomenon at the end of the day

definitions.text: a phenomenon at the end of the day

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected means gathered again into a new order

explanation.surface: Marilyn Monroe is remembered as a sensation of her day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembering, but split as re-collected it means the letters are gathered again in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon often appears above the horizon at dusk, an evening event in the sky.

clue.text: Get home by boat when on a trip

indicators.note: on a trip suggests the letters are stumbling about out of order

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Getting back home by boat after a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire or procure something is to get it, so these are synonyms.

clue.text: Article inferior to joke that's cracked

indicators.note: inferior to means lower down, so in this down clue the article sits beneath the joke

parts.note: a gag is a joke
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article less funny than a joke that fell flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracked in the sense of crazy or mentally unhinged is a synonym of senile or dotty.

clue.text: Diamonds, perhaps, in case

definitions.meaning: diamonds are one of the four groups in a pack of cards
a case in court, a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Jewels kept safely in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a group of playing cards such as diamonds and also a legal action brought in court.

clue.text: Good-humoured remark ultimately distasteful among simple folk

indicators.note: among says the single letter is placed in the midst of the folk word

parts.note: the peasantry are country people of humble rank

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the final letter of the word distasteful

explanation.surface: A joke that turns out to be in poor taste among country people.
explanation.definitionFit: A light joke or polite friendly comment is a good-humoured remark.

clue.text: Old habit past, time to make a comeback

indicators.note: to make a comeback means the letters return, read backwards

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: An outdated custom from the past is due to return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' suggests a custom; it is a garment, as a nun's habit is.
explanation.definitionFit: Habit can mean a garment, and the loose robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome is an old one.

clue.text: President waving red flag, or leader of democracy?

indicators.note: a waving flag flaps about, so these letters are tossed into a new order
leader of asks for the opening letter of the word democracy

explanation.surface: Does a president wave a socialist red flag, or lead democracy?
explanation.definitionFit: He was the thirty-eighth US head of state, serving 1974-77 after Nixon resigned.
